title: Right-triangle trigonometry and special angles
section: Trigonometry ▷ Trig Functions of Acute Angles
terms: sine; cosine; tangent; cosecant; secant; cotangent; hypotenuse; complementary angles; cofunctions; special right triangle.

exposition.text:
For an acute angle in a right triangle, sine is opposite over hypotenuse, cosine adjacent over
hypotenuse, and tangent opposite over adjacent. Cosecant, secant, and cotangent are the recip-
rocals of sine, cosine, and tangent, respectively. Complementary angles add to π/2; their sine
and cosine values are exchanged, as are tangent and cotangent, secant and cosecant.
√ √
The 45-45-90 triangle has side ratio 1 : 1 : 2, and the 30-60-90 triangle has ratio 1 : 3 : 2.
These give exact values at π/6, π/4, and π/3. Always interpret “opposite” relative to the cho-
sen angle, and use a unitless ratio rather than an angle measure as the value of a trig function.

question.text:
In a right triangle, an acute angle θ satisfies tan θ + cot θ = 5. What is sin θ cos θ?
√
(A) 1/10 (B) 1/5 (C) 2/5 (D) 1/2 (E) 5/5

solution.text:
2 2
tan θ + cot θ = (sin θ + cos θ)/(sin θ cos θ) = 1/(sin θ cos θ). Hence the desired product is
1/5.

question.text:
The altitude to the hypotenuse of a right triangle divides that hypotenuse into segments of
lengths 1 and 3. What is the sine of the smaller acute angle?
√ √ √
(A) 1/4 (B) 1/2 (C) 3/2 (D) 3/4 (E) 1/ 3

solution.text:
The hypotenuse has length 4. By similarity, the squares of the legs are 4 · 1 and 4 · 3, so the
shorter leg is 2. The smaller angle is opposite that leg, and its sine is 2/4 = 1/2.

question.text:
A right triangle has hypotenuse 13 and inradius 2. What is its area?
(A) 30 (B) 36 (C) 26 (D) 32 (E) 24

solution.text:
2 2 2
If the legs are a, b, then a + b = 13 + 4 = 17. Since a + b = 169, 2ab = 17 − 169 = 120, so
the area is ab/2 = 30.

(A) 4/9 (B) 1/5 (C) 1/3 (D) 2/9 (E) 2/5

solution.text:

2/9.
